description.narrative: Stage III implementation focuses on the refrigeration servicing sector, as there is no longer production in the refrigeration or foam sectors in Jordan. The sector's consumption is primarily driven by high leakage rates from old equipment, a lack of regulations governing maintenance frequency and prevention of venting into the atmosphere, and the under-developed recovery and recycling systems initiated under Stage II, which require further development in Stage III. To address these issues, Stage III includes targeted activities aimed at enhancing the capacity of refrigeration technicians to ensure proper servicing of refrigeration technologies and safe handling of low-global-warming-potential (GWP) refrigerants, improving the capacity for recovery, recycling, and reuse of refrigerants, strengthening customs' ability to control HCFCs, increasing awareness and participation in HPMP activities, and phasing out HCFC-22 in cold storage facilities. Rather than spreading resources across numerous small activities, Jordan has opted to focus on a s treamlined set of initiatives that align with Stage I of the Kigali Implementation Plan (KIP) for effective execution.
